$comment: Global tuning surface. Everything the engine reads at runtime lives here; no engine edit should ever be needed to rebalance the game. Times are in LOGIC FRAMES at 60Hz unless the key says 'Seconds'. Distances are world units (a fighter is ~1.8 tall).

timestep.$comment: Logic runs at a fixed 60Hz. maxCatchUpSteps caps how many logic steps one render frame may consume, so a tab that was backgrounded resumes instead of spiral-of-deathing.

stage.$comment: Fighters are clamped to +/- halfWidth. Hitting the wall is what makes corner pressure real.

physics.$comment: pushApart keeps two bodies from occupying the same space; each fighter is displaced half the overlap, and the corner clamp then wins so you can be pinned.

hitstop.$comment: Freeze both fighters for min..max frames, lerped by damage. A jab barely stutters; a special slams.

shake.$comment: Only hits at or above heavyDamageThreshold shake the camera, so jabs stay readable.

input.$comment: Attacks fire on the press, not while held. A press opens a buffer this many frames wide, consumed when the move actually starts — so an attack pressed slightly before recovery ends still comes out. Set to 0 for strict frame-perfect input.

camera.$comment: Camera tracks the midpoint of both fighters and pulls back as they separate.

ai.$comment: reactionFrames is how long the AI takes to notice a startup before it can react-block — lower is harder.

phaseLerp.$comment: The feel of the whole game lives in these four numbers. strike snaps onto the pose on active frames; recovery settles slowly out of it.

animation.$comment: useClips=false forces the procedural poser even when retargeted clips loaded — handy for A/B-ing feel.
